\chapter{Water and Rice}
\label{ch:ml-water-and-rice}

This chapter is generated from the canonical micro-lessons used by Language Ladder.
Each section stays independently resumable and preserves the authored prerequisite order.

\section[\ml{വെള്ളം} \ml{അരി} \ml{ചോറ്}]{\ml{വെള്ളം}, \ml{അരി}, \ml{ചോറ്} — a different water-word, the same rice-words}

\label{lesson:ML-C15-vellam-ari}



\begin{quote}
\textbf{Warm-up.} {[}PAUSE 2s{]} For once, Malayalam's everyday word for something basic genuinely \textbf{doesn't} match Tamil's — even though water is about as basic as vocabulary gets.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know}
\textbf{\ml{വെള്ളം}} (\emph{veḷḷam}) = "\textbf{water}" — and notably, this is \textbf{not} built on \emph{nīr} the way Tamil's \emph{taṇṇīr} is. Instead, \emph{veḷḷam} shares the \textbf{\ml{വെൾ}} (\emph{veḷ-}, "\textbf{bright, white}") root you already met in \emph{veḷḷi}, "silver/ Venus," from the colors and days lessons — \emph{veḷḷam} originally meant something closer to "\textbf{flood, deluge}" before becoming Malayalam's plain, everyday word for water. (\emph{Nīr} itself hasn't vanished from Malayalam — it survives inside compounds like \textbf{\ml{ഇളനീർ}} \emph{iḷanīr}, "tender coconut water," and \textbf{\ml{കണ്ണീർ}} \emph{kaṇṇīr}, "tears" — it's just not the standalone everyday word anymore.)

\begin{cousinweb}
Rice, though, tells the familiar story:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textbf{\ml{അരി}} (\emph{ari}) = "\textbf{rice}" (raw grain) — closely matching Tamil \emph{arisi}.
  \item \textbf{\ml{ചോറ്}} (\emph{cōṟu}) = "\textbf{cooked rice}" (the meal) — and here Malayalam actually \textbf{does} have a Tamil cognate: Tamil keeps its own native \textbf{\ta{சோறு}} (also \emph{cōṟu}), used alongside the Sanskrit-influenced \emph{sātam} as an everyday near-synonym. Malayalam simply made \emph{cōṟu} its main word, where Tamil more often reaches for \emph{sātam}.
\end{itemize}
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{Guided Practice}
{[}PAUSE 1s{]}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item {[}YOU SAY: "veḷḷam" — water, NOT matching Tamil's neer{]}
  \item {[}YOU SAY: "ari" — raw rice, matching Tamil closely{]}
  \item {[}YOU SAY: "cōṟu" — cooked rice, Malayalam's own word{]}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Wrap-up recall}]
{[}PAUSE 3s{]} Does Malayalam's everyday water-word match Tamil's? (\textbf{No} — \emph{veḷḷam} shares the \emph{veḷ-} "bright/white" root instead, originally meaning "flood"; though \emph{nīr} itself survives in compounds like \emph{iḷanīr} and \emph{kaṇṇīr}.) Does its raw-rice word match Tamil's? (\textbf{Yes} — \emph{ari} closely matches \emph{arisi}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
